name_translation: The Yoga of the Threefold Division of Faith

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
ये शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य यजन्ते श्रद्धयान्विताः |
तेषां निष्ठा तु का कृष्ण सत्त्वमाहो रजस्तमः || १ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
ये शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य यजन्ते श्रद्धयान्विताः |
तेषां निष्ठा तु का कृष्ण सत्त्वमाहो रजस्तमः || १ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
ye śāstravidhimutsṛjya yajante śraddhayānvitāḥ |
teṣāṃ niṣṭhā tu kā kṛṣṇa sattvamāho rajastamaḥ || 1 ||
verses.word_meanings: arjunaḥ uvāca—Arjuna said; ye—those who; śāstra-vidhim—the ordinances and rules of scripture; utsṛjya—setting aside/ignoring; yajante—perform sacrifice/worship; śraddhayā-anvitāḥ—endowed with faith; teṣām—their; niṣṭhā—state of faith / status; tu—indeed; kā—what is; kṛṣṇa—O Krishna; sattvam—Sattva (goodness); āho—or; rajaḥ—Rajas (passion); tamaḥ—Tamas (ignorance).
verses.translation: Arjuna said: Those who, setting aside the scriptural injunctions, perform worship and sacrifice endowed with faith—what is their true spiritual state, O Krishna? Is it of the nature of Sattva, Rajas, or Tamas?
verses.meaning: Arjuna presents a critical practical question: If a person lacks scriptural knowledge or disobeys scriptural procedures, yet worships with sincere inner faith, what is the quality and outcome of that worship?
verses.purport: Arjuna presents a critical practical question: If a person lacks scriptural knowledge or disobeys scriptural procedures, yet worships with sincere inner faith, what is the quality and outcome of that worship?

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
त्रिविधा भवति श्रद्धा देहिनां सा स्वभावजा |
सात्त्विकी राजसी चैव तामसी चेति तां शृणु || २ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
त्रिविधा भवति श्रद्धा देहिनां सा स्वभावजा |
सात्त्विकी राजसी चैव तामसी चेति तां शृणु || २ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
trividhā bhavati śraddhā dehināṃ sā svabhāvajā |
sāttvikī rājasī caiva tāmasī ceti tāṃ śṛṇu || 2 ||
verses.word_meanings: śrī-bhagavān uvāca—the Supreme Lord said; tri-vidhā—threefold; bhavati—is; śraddhā—faith; dehinām—of the embodied souls; sā—that; svabhāva-jā—born of one's innate nature/past impressions; sāttvikī—Sattvic (in goodness); rājasī—Rajasic (in passion); ca eva—and also; tāmasī—Tamasic (in ignorance); ca iti—and thus; tām—about that; śṛṇu—now hear.
verses.translation: The Supreme Lord said: The faith of embodied beings is threefold, arising from their innate past impressions (Svabhava)—Sattvic, Rajasic, and Tamasic. Listen now as I explain this.
verses.meaning: Faith is not a random or uniform quality; it reflects the dominant guna of an individual's subtle mind (Samskaras accumulated across past lives). Thus, faith expresses itself in three distinct modes.
verses.purport: Faith is not a random or uniform quality; it reflects the dominant guna of an individual's subtle mind (Samskaras accumulated across past lives). Thus, faith expresses itself in three distinct modes.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत |
श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः || ३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत |
श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः || ३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
sattvānurūpā sarvasya śraddhā bhavati bhārata |
śraddhāmayo'yaṃ puruṣo yo yacchraddhaḥ sa eva saḥ || 3 ||
verses.word_meanings: sattva-anurūpā—conforming to the purity of the inner mind; sarvasya—of everyone; śraddhā—faith; bhavati—is; bhārata—O descendant of Bharata (Arjuna); śraddhā-mayaḥ—constituted of faith; ayam—this; puruṣaḥ—human being / soul; yaḥ—whoever; yat-śraddhaḥ—whatever his faith is; saḥ eva saḥ—he indeed is that.
verses.translation: The faith of every individual corresponds to the inner disposition of their mind, O Bharata. A person is formed of their faith; whatever one's faith is, that indeed is what that person is.
verses.meaning: This is one of the profoundest psychological insights of the Gita: 'Shraddhamayo 'yam purusho'. Faith is the core operating system of consciousness. What you trust, revere, and value determines your character, choices, and destiny.
verses.purport: This is one of the profoundest psychological insights of the Gita: 'Shraddhamayo 'yam purusho'. Faith is the core operating system of consciousness. What you trust, revere, and value determines your character, choices, and destiny.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यजन्ते सात्त्विका देवान्यक्षरक्षांसि राजसाः |
प्रेतान्भूतगणांश्चान्ये यजन्ते तामसा जनाः || ४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यजन्ते सात्त्विका देवान्यक्षरक्षांसि राजसाः |
प्रेतान्भूतगणांश्चान्ये यजन्ते तामसा जनाः || ४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yajante sāttvikā devānyakṣarakṣāṃsi rājasāḥ |
pretānbhūtagaṇāṃścānye yajante tāmasā janāḥ || 4 ||
verses.word_meanings: yajante—worship; sāttvikāḥ—persons in the mode of goodness; devān—the celestial demigods (Devas); yakṣa-rakṣāṃsi—the Yakshas and Rakshasas (beings of wealth, power, and fierce passions); rājasāḥ—persons in the mode of passion; pretān—departed spirits/ghosts; bhūta-gaṇān—the elemental hordes / spirits; ca—and; anye—others; yajante—worship; tāmasāḥ janāḥ—people in the mode of ignorance.
verses.translation: Men in the mode of goodness worship the celestial Devas; those in the mode of passion worship powerful Yakshas and fierce Rakshasas; while those in the mode of ignorance worship ghosts and elemental spirits.
verses.meaning: The object of one's adoration reveals one's inner guna: Sattvic minds worship luminous cosmic devas; Rajasic minds seek wealth and occult power through fiercer deities; Tamasic minds gravitate toward morbid spiritism and black magic.
verses.purport: The object of one's adoration reveals one's inner guna: Sattvic minds worship luminous cosmic devas; Rajasic minds seek wealth and occult power through fiercer deities; Tamasic minds gravitate toward morbid spiritism and black magic.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अशास्त्रविहितं घोरं तप्यन्ते ये तपो जनाः |
दम्भाहङ्कारसंयुक्ताः कामरागबलान्विताः || ५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अशास्त्रविहितं घोरं तप्यन्ते ये तपो जनाः |
दम्भाहङ्कारसंयुक्ताः कामरागबलान्विताः || ५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
aśāstravihitaṃ ghoraṃ tapyante ye tapo janāḥ |
dambhāhaṅkārasaṃyuktāḥ kāmarāgabalānvitāḥ || 5 ||
verses.word_meanings: a-śāstra-vihitam—not sanctioned by scriptural wisdom; ghoram—severe and dreadful; tapyante—undergo; ye—those who; tapaḥ—austerity/penance; janāḥ—people; dambha-ahaṅkāra-saṃyuktāḥ—accompanied by ostentation and pride; kāma-rāga-bala-anvitāḥ—impelled by the force of lust, attachment, and ego.
verses.translation: Those people who practice severe, unscriptural austerities out of hypocrisy and egotism, driven by the violent urge of lust and personal attachment;
verses.meaning: Extreme mortification of the flesh performed for showmanship or egoic power is not genuine spiritual discipline, but a distorted perversion driven by pride.
verses.purport: Extreme mortification of the flesh performed for showmanship or egoic power is not genuine spiritual discipline, but a distorted perversion driven by pride.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
कर्षयन्तः शरीरस्थं भूतग्राममचेतसः |
मां चैवान्तःशरीरस्थं तान्विद्ध्यासुरनिश्चयान् || ६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
कर्षयन्तः शरीरस्थं भूतग्राममचेतसः |
मां चैवान्तःशरीरस्थं तान्विद्ध्यासुरनिश्चयान् || ६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
karṣayantaḥ śarīrasthaṃ bhūtagrāmamacetasaḥ |
māṃ caivāntaḥśarīrasthaṃ tānviddhyāsuraniścayān || 6 ||
verses.word_meanings: karṣayantaḥ—tormenting/torturing; śarīra-stham—situated in the body; bhūta-grāmam—the aggregate of physical elements and organs; acetasaḥ—senseless/foolish; mām—Me; ca eva—and also; antaḥ-śarīra-stham—dwelling within the heart of the body; tān—them; viddhi—know; āsura-niścayān—to be of demonic resolve.
verses.translation: Senselessly tormenting the bodily organs and physical elements within them, and tormenting Me who dwell as the indwelling Lord within their hearts—know them to be of demonic resolve.
verses.meaning: The body is the living temple of the Paramatman. Cruel, unnatural self-torture is an offense against the indwelling Divine presence.
verses.purport: The body is the living temple of the Paramatman. Cruel, unnatural self-torture is an offense against the indwelling Divine presence.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
आहारस्त्वपि सर्वस्य त्रिविधो भवति प्रियः |
यज्ञस्तपस्तथा दानं तेषां भेदमिमं शृणु || ७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
आहारस्त्वपि सर्वस्य त्रिविधो भवति प्रियः |
यज्ञस्तपस्तथा दानं तेषां भेदमिमं शृणु || ७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
āhārastvapi sarvasya trividho bhavati priyaḥ |
yajñastapastathā dānaṃ teṣāṃ bhedamimaṃ śṛṇu || 7 ||
verses.word_meanings: āhāraḥ—food; tu api—even; sarvasya—of everyone; tri-vidhaḥ—threefold; bhavati—is; priyaḥ—dear/preferred; yajñaḥ—sacrifice; tapaḥ—austerity; tathā—as well as; dānam—charity; teṣām—of them; bhedam imam—this distinction; śṛṇu—now hear.
verses.translation: Even the food preferred by everyone is of three distinct kinds. Likewise, sacrifice (Yajna), austerity (Tapas), and charity (Dana) are each threefold. Hear now their distinctions.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna transitions to analyze the four pillars of daily human conduct: Diet (Ahara), Worship/Sacrifice (Yajna), Discipline (Tapas), and Philanthropy (Dana) across the three gunas.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna transitions to analyze the four pillars of daily human conduct: Diet (Ahara), Worship/Sacrifice (Yajna), Discipline (Tapas), and Philanthropy (Dana) across the three gunas.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
आयुःसत्त्वबलारोग्यसुखप्रीतिविवर्धनाः |
रस्याः स्निग्धाः स्थिरा हृद्या आहाराः सात्त्विकप्रियाः || ८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
आयुःसत्त्वबलारोग्यसुखप्रीतिविवर्धनाः |
रस्याः स्निग्धाः स्थिरा हृद्या आहाराः सात्त्विकप्रियाः || ८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
āyuḥsattvabalārogyasukhaprītivivardhanāḥ |
rasyāḥ snigdhāḥ sthirā hṛdyā āhārāḥ sāttvikapriyāḥ || 8 ||
verses.word_meanings: āyuḥ—lifespan; sattva—purity of mind and vitality; bala—physical strength; ārogya—health and freedom from disease; sukha—happiness; prīti—inner cheerfulness; vivardhanāḥ—enhancing/increasing; rasyāḥ—juicy and flavorful; snigdhāḥ—wholesome and unctuous (with healthy natural fats); sthirāḥ—substantive and sustaining; hṛdyāḥ—agreeable to the heart/palate; āhārāḥ—foods; sāttvika-priyāḥ—dear to the Sattvic.
verses.translation: Foods that promote longevity, mental purity, physical strength, health, happiness, and cheerfulness, and which are juicy, wholesome, sustaining, and agreeable to the heart, are dear to those in the mode of goodness (Sattva).
verses.meaning: Sattvic food nourishes both the physical body and the subtle cognitive faculties: fresh vegetables, fruits, whole grains, dairy, nuts, and naturally cooked meals that foster inner serenity and vitality.
verses.purport: Sattvic food nourishes both the physical body and the subtle cognitive faculties: fresh vegetables, fruits, whole grains, dairy, nuts, and naturally cooked meals that foster inner serenity and vitality.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
कट्वम्ललवणात्युष्णतीक्ष्णरूक्षविदाहिनः |
आहारा राजसस्येष्टा दुःखशोकामयप्रदाः || ९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
कट्वम्ललवणात्युष्णतीक्ष्णरूक्षविदाहिनः |
आहारा राजसस्येष्टा दुःखशोकामयप्रदाः || ९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
kaṭvamlalavaṇātyuṣṇatīkṣṇarūkṣavidāhinaḥ |
āhārā rājasasyeṣṭā duḥkhaśokāmayapradāḥ || 9 ||
verses.word_meanings: kaṭu—excessively bitter; amla—excessively sour; lavaṇa—excessively salty; ati-uṣṇa—excessively hot/spicy; tīkṣṇa—pungent/burning; rūkṣa—harsh and dry; vidāhinaḥ—causing inflammation and burning sensation; āhārāḥ—foods; rājasasya iṣṭāḥ—desired by the passionate (Rajasic); duḥkha-śoka-āmaya-pradāḥ—producing distress, depression, and disease.
verses.translation: Foods that are excessively bitter, sour, salty, intensely hot, pungent, dry, and burning are dear to those in the mode of passion (Rajas), causing distress, grief, and disease.
verses.meaning: Overly stimulating foods agitate the nervous system and trigger restlessness, inflammatory ailments, digestive disorders, and emotional volatility.
verses.purport: Overly stimulating foods agitate the nervous system and trigger restlessness, inflammatory ailments, digestive disorders, and emotional volatility.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यातयामं गतरसं पूति पर्युषितं च यत् |
उच्छिष्टमपि चामेध्यं भोजनं तामसप्रियम् || १० ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यातयामं गतरसं पूति पर्युषितं च यत् |
उच्छिष्टमपि चामेध्यं भोजनं तामसप्रियम् || १० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yātayāmaṃ gatarasaṃ pūti paryuṣitaṃ ca yat |
ucchiṣṭamapi cāmedhyaṃ bhojanaṃ tāmasapriyam || 10 ||
verses.word_meanings: yāta-yāmam—cooked hours before / stale; gata-rasam—tasteless / devoid of life energy (Prana); pūti—foul-smelling/putrid; paryuṣitam—fermented or decomposed; ca yat—and that which; ucchiṣṭam—unclean remnants/scraps; api ca—and also; amedhyam—impure / unfit for consumption; bhojanam—food/meal; tāmasa-priyam—dear to those in the mode of ignorance (Tamas).
verses.translation: Food that is cooked hours beforehand, devoid of flavor and vitality, putrid, decomposed, stale remnants, and contaminated—such food is dear to those in the mode of ignorance (Tamas).
verses.meaning: Tamasic foods (dead, processed, foul, intoxicating, or rotten substances) induce lethargy, depression, mental darkness, and chronic physical degeneration.
verses.purport: Tamasic foods (dead, processed, foul, intoxicating, or rotten substances) induce lethargy, depression, mental darkness, and chronic physical degeneration.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्यज्ञो विधिदृष्टो य इज्यते |
यष्टव्यमेवेति मनः समाधाय स सात्त्विकः || ११ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्यज्ञो विधिदृष्टो य इज्यते |
यष्टव्यमेवेति मनः समाधाय स सात्त्विकः || ११ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
aphaiākāṅkṣibhiryajño vidhidṛṣṭo ya ijyate |
yaṣṭavyameveti manaḥ samādhāya sa sāttvikaḥ || 11 ||
verses.word_meanings: aphala-ākāṅkṣibhiḥ—by those devoid of desire for fruits/rewards; yajñaḥ—sacrifice; vidhi-dṛṣṭaḥ—directed by scriptural injunctions; yaḥ—which; ijyate—is performed; yaṣṭavyam eva iti—duty to be performed for its own sake; manaḥ—mind; samādhāya—firmly fixing; saḥ—that; sāttvikaḥ—is Sattvic (in the mode of goodness).
verses.translation: That sacrifice which is offered according to scriptural ordinances by persons desiring no reward, with a mind firmly resolved that sacrifice is a sacred duty, is Sattvic.
verses.meaning: A Sattvic Yajna is performed purely as an offering to God (Nishkama Karma) without selfish bargaining, in strict alignment with sacred spiritual principles.
verses.purport: A Sattvic Yajna is performed purely as an offering to God (Nishkama Karma) without selfish bargaining, in strict alignment with sacred spiritual principles.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अभिसन्धाय तु फलं दम्भार्थमपि चैव यत् |
इज्यते भरतश्रेष्ठ तं यज्ञं विद्धि राजसम् || १२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अभिसन्धाय तु फलं दम्भार्थमपि चैव यत् |
इज्यते भरतश्रेष्ठ तं यज्ञं विद्धि राजसम् || १२ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
abhisandhāya tu phalaṃ dambhārthamapi caiva yat |
ijyate bharataśreṣṭha taṃ yajñaṃ viddhi rājasam || 12 ||
verses.word_meanings: abhisandhāya—aiming at / desiring; tu—but; phalam—fruit/reward; dambha-artham—for the sake of show and prestige; api ca eva—and also indeed; yat—which; ijyate—is performed; bharata-śreṣṭha—O best of Bharatas; tam yajñam—that sacrifice; viddhi—know; rājasam—to be Rajasic.
verses.translation: But that sacrifice which is offered seeking a specific reward, or for the sake of ostentatious display, O best of the Bharatas, know that sacrifice to be Rajasic.
verses.meaning: When rituals and charitable works are conducted to acquire fame, power, or social standing, they fall under the mode of passion.
verses.purport: When rituals and charitable works are conducted to acquire fame, power, or social standing, they fall under the mode of passion.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
विधिहीनमसृष्टान्नं मन्त्रहीनमदक्षिणम् |
श्रद्धाविरहितं यज्ञं तामसं परिचक्षते || १३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
विधिहीनमसृष्टान्नं मन्त्रहीनमदक्षिणम् |
श्रद्धाविरहितं यज्ञं तामसं परिचक्षते || १३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
vidhihīnamasṛṣṭānnaṃ mantrahīnamadakṣiṇam |
śraddhāvirahitaṃ yajñaṃ tāmasaṃ paricakṣate || 13 ||
verses.word_meanings: vidhi-hīnam—without scriptural authority; asṛṣṭa-annam—without distribution of sanctified food (Prasada); mantra-hīnam—devoid of sacred chants; adakṣiṇam—without honoring priests/teachers; śraddhā-virahitam—devoid of faith; yajñam—sacrifice; tāmasam—Tamasic; paricakṣate—is declared.
verses.translation: A sacrifice performed contrary to scriptural guidelines, where no sanctified food is distributed, no sacred mantras are chanted, no respect or honorarium is given, and which is devoid of faith, is declared to be Tamasic.
verses.meaning: Tamasic ritualism is careless, irreverent, and stingy, offering no benefit to the practitioner or society.
verses.purport: Tamasic ritualism is careless, irreverent, and stingy, offering no benefit to the practitioner or society.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
देवद्विजगुरुप्राज्ञपूजनं शौचमार्जवम् |
ब्रह्मचर्यमहिंसा च शारीरं तप उच्यते || १४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
देवद्विजगुरुप्राज्ञपूजनं शौचमार्जवम् |
ब्रह्मचर्यमहिंसा च शारीरं तप उच्यते || १४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
devadvijaguruprājñapūjanaṃ śaucamārjavam |
brahmacaryamahiṃsā ca śārīraṃ tapa ucyate || 14 ||
verses.word_meanings: deva—the Supreme Lord and deities; dvija—the wise and twice-born; guru—spiritual preceptors; prājña—the enlightened sages; pūjanam—worship and reverence; śaucam—cleanliness of body; ārjavam—straightforwardness; brahmacaryam—continence/chastity; ahiṃsā ca—and non-injury; śārīram—bodily/physical; tapaḥ—austerity; ucyate—is declared.
verses.translation: Worship of the Supreme Divine, the pure-hearted, the spiritual masters, and the enlightened sages; cleanliness, straightforwardness, celibacy/continence, and non-violence—this is declared to be physical/bodily austerity (Sharira Tapas).
verses.meaning: True physical austerity is not self-mortification, but directing the physical body into reverent service, ethical purity, self-restraint, and universal harmlessness.
verses.purport: True physical austerity is not self-mortification, but directing the physical body into reverent service, ethical purity, self-restraint, and universal harmlessness.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् |
स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते || १५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् |
स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते || १५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
anudvegakaraṃ vākyaṃ satyaṃ priyahitaṃ ca yat |
svādhyāyābhyasanaṃ caiva vāṅmayaṃ tapa ucyate || 15 ||
verses.word_meanings: anudvega-karam—causing no agitation or distress; vākyam—speech/words; satyam—truthful; priya-hitam ca yat—which is pleasing and beneficial; svādhyāya-abhyasanam—the regular recitation and study of sacred scriptures; ca eva—and also; vāṅ-mayam—of the voice/speech; tapaḥ—austerity; ucyate—is declared.
verses.translation: Speech that causes no agitation, which is truthful, pleasant, and beneficial, combined with the regular chanting and contemplation of sacred scriptures—this is declared to be verbal austerity (Vangmaya Tapas).
verses.meaning: This classic verse sets the gold standard for communication: Words must satisfy four concurrent tests—non-injurious (Anudvega-kara), true (Satya), agreeable (Priya), and constructive/uplifting (Hita).
verses.purport: This classic verse sets the gold standard for communication: Words must satisfy four concurrent tests—non-injurious (Anudvega-kara), true (Satya), agreeable (Priya), and constructive/uplifting (Hita).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मनःप्रसादः सौम्यत्वं मौनमात्मविनिग्रहः |
भावसंशुद्धिरित्येतत्तपो मानसमुच्यते || १६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मनःप्रसादः सौम्यत्वं मौनमात्मविनिग्रहः |
भावसंशुद्धिरित्येतत्तपो मानसमुच्यते || १६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
manaḥprasādaḥ saamyatvaṃ maunamātmavinigrahaḥ |
bhāvasaṃśuddhirityetattapo mānasamucyate || 16 ||
verses.word_meanings: manaḥ-prasādaḥ—serenity and cheerfulness of mind; saamyatvam—gentleness/kindness; maunam—inner silence and contemplation; ātma-vinigrahaḥ—self-control / mastering the wandering thoughts; bhāva-saṃśuddhiḥ—purity of emotional intent; iti etat—all this; tapaḥ mānasam—mental austerity; ucyate—is declared.
verses.translation: Serenity of mind, gentleness, inner silence and reflection, self-mastery, and absolute purity of heart and intent—this is declared to be mental austerity (Manasa Tapas).
verses.meaning: Mental discipline is the crown of spiritual practice: Cultivating cheerful equilibrium, kindness, silencing inner chattering, and purifying all motives from selfish taint.
verses.purport: Mental discipline is the crown of spiritual practice: Cultivating cheerful equilibrium, kindness, silencing inner chattering, and purifying all motives from selfish taint.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
श्रद्धया परया तप्तं तपस्तत्त्रिविधं नरैः |
अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्युक्तैः सात्त्विकं परिचक्षते || १७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
श्रद्धया परया तप्तं तपस्तत्त्रिविधं नरैः |
अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्युक्तैः सात्त्विकं परिचक्षते || १७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
śraddhayā parayā taptaṃ tapastattrividhaṃ naraiḥ |
aphaiākāṅkṣibhiryuktaiḥ sāttvikaṃ paricakṣate || 17 ||
verses.word_meanings: śraddhayā parayā—with supreme transcendent faith; taptam—practiced; tapaḥ—austerity; tat tri-vidham—that threefold (body, speech, mind); naraiḥ—by persons; aphala-ākāṅkṣibhiḥ—desiring no personal fruit/reward; yuktaiḥ—disciplined and steadfast; sāttvikam—Sattvic; paricakṣate—is declared.
verses.translation: This threefold austerity of body, speech, and mind, practiced with supreme faith by disciplined seekers desiring no personal reward, is declared to be Sattvic.
verses.meaning: When physical, verbal, and mental disciplines are practiced with deep faith and surrender to God, they elevate consciousness into pure Sattva.
verses.purport: When physical, verbal, and mental disciplines are practiced with deep faith and surrender to God, they elevate consciousness into pure Sattva.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सत्कारमानपूजार्थं तपो दम्बेन चैव यत् |
क्रियते तदिह प्रोक्तं राजसं चलमध्रुवम् || १८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सत्कारमानपूजार्थं तपो दम्बेन चैव यत् |
क्रियते तदिह प्रोक्तं राजसं चलमध्रुवम् || १८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
satkāramānapūjārthaṃ tapo dambhena caiva yat |
kriyate tadiha proktaṃ rājasaṃ calamadhruvam || 18 ||
verses.word_meanings: satkāra—respect and acclaim; māna—honor; pūjā-artham—for the sake of receiving adoration; tapaḥ—austerity; dambhena—with ostentation/hypocrisy; ca eva—and also; yat—which; kriyate—is performed; tat—that; iha—here; proktam—is declared; rājasam—Rajasic; calam—fickle/unstable; adhruvam—temporary and ephemeral.
verses.translation: That austerity which is performed with ostentation for the purpose of gaining acclaim, honor, and public praise is declared to be Rajasic—unstable and fleeting in its results.
verses.meaning: Practicing penance to impress others or to acquire spiritual guru status yields only short-lived worldly acclaim with no lasting spiritual benefit.
verses.purport: Practicing penance to impress others or to acquire spiritual guru status yields only short-lived worldly acclaim with no lasting spiritual benefit.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मूढग्राहेणात्मनो यत्पीडया क्रियते तपः |
परस्योत्सादनार्थं वा तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् || १९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मूढग्राहेणात्मनो यत्पीडया क्रियते तपः |
परस्योत्सादनार्थं वा तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् || १९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
mūḍhagrāheṇātmano yatpīḍayā kriyate tapaḥ |
parasyotsādanārthaṃ vā tattāmasamudāhṛtam || 19 ||
verses.word_meanings: mūḍha-grāheṇa—out of foolish stubbornness and delusion; ātmanaḥ—of oneself; yat—which; pīḍayā—with painful self-torture; kriyate—is performed; tapaḥ—austerity; parasya—of others; utsādana-artham—for the ruin and destruction; vā—or; tat—that; tāmasam—Tamasic; udāhṛtam—is exemplified.
verses.translation: That austerity which is performed out of foolish stubbornness, with painful self-torture, or for the purpose of harming and destroying others, is declared to be Tamasic.
verses.meaning: Tamasic austerity is characterized by fanatical self-harm (e.g., severe mutilation) or sinister rituals intended to inflict harm on enemies.
verses.purport: Tamasic austerity is characterized by fanatical self-harm (e.g., severe mutilation) or sinister rituals intended to inflict harm on enemies.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
दातव्यमिति यद्दानं दीयतेऽनुपकारिणे |
देशे काले च पात्रे च तद्दानं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम् || २० ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
दातव्यमिति यद्दानं दीयतेऽनुपकारिणे |
देशे काले च पात्रे च तद्दानं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम् || २० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
dātavyamiti yaddānaṃ dīyate'nupakāriṇe |
deśe kāle ca pātre ca taddānaṃ sāttvikaṃ smṛtam || 20 ||
verses.word_meanings: dātavyam iti—it is a sacred duty to give; yat dānam—which charity; dīyate—is given; anupakāriṇe—to one who can render no service in return; deśe—in a holy/suitable place; kāle—at an auspicious time; ca—and; pātre—to a worthy and deserving recipient; ca—and; tat dānam—that gift; sāttvikam—Sattvic; smṛtam—is regarded.
verses.translation: That charity which is given as a sacred duty, with no expectation of any return favor, in a proper place, at an auspicious time, and to a worthy recipient, is regarded as Sattvic.
verses.meaning: Sattvic charity (Dana) is pure grace: It expects no reciprocity, respects the dignity of the recipient, and ensures that the aid genuinely uplifts a deserving cause.
verses.purport: Sattvic charity (Dana) is pure grace: It expects no reciprocity, respects the dignity of the recipient, and ensures that the aid genuinely uplifts a deserving cause.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यत्तु प्रत्युपकारार्थं फलमुद्दिश्य वा पुनः |
दीयते च परिक्लिष्टं तद्दानं राजसं स्मृतम् || २१ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यत्तु प्रत्युपकारार्थं फलमुद्दिश्य वा पुनः |
दीयते च परिक्लिष्टं तद्दानं राजसं स्मृतम् || २१ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yattu pratyupakārārthaṃ phalamuddiśya vā punaḥ |
dīyate ca parikliṣṭaṃ taddānaṃ rājasaṃ smṛtam || 21 ||
verses.word_meanings: yat tu—that which indeed; prati-upakāra-artham—with the intention of receiving a return favor; phalam—fruit/reward; uddiśya—aiming at; vā punaḥ—or again; dīyate—is given; ca—and; parikliṣṭam—grudgingly / with pain of parting with wealth; tat dānam—that charity; rājasam—Rajasic; smṛtam—is declared.
verses.translation: But that charity which is given with the expectation of a return favor, or looking for personal gain, or given grudgingly and with regret, is regarded as Rajasic.
verses.meaning: Transactional charity or giving with a heavy heart tainted by attachment turns an act of benevolence into a business deal.
verses.purport: Transactional charity or giving with a heavy heart tainted by attachment turns an act of benevolence into a business deal.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अदेशकाले यद्दानमपात्रेभ्यश्च दीयते |
असत्कृतमवज्ञातं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् || २२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अदेशकाले यद्दानमपात्रेभ्यश्च दीयते |
असत्कृतमवज्ञातं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् || २२ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
adeśakāle yaddānamapātrebhyaśca dīyate |
asatkṛtamavajñātaṃ tattāmasamudāhṛtam || 22 ||
verses.word_meanings: a-deśa-kāle—at an improper place and unholy time; yat dānam—which charity; apātrebhyaḥ—to unworthy and corrupt recipients; ca—and; dīyate—is given; asatkṛtam—without basic respect; avajñātam—with insult and contempt; tat—that; tāmasam—Tamasic; udāhṛtam—is exemplified.
verses.translation: Charity that is given at an improper place and time, to unworthy recipients who misuse it, or given disrespectfully with arrogance and contempt, is declared to be Tamasic.
verses.meaning: Funding destructive vices (like drugs or gambling) or throwing money at beggars with contempt constitutes Tamasic giving, causing negative karmic reactions.
verses.purport: Funding destructive vices (like drugs or gambling) or throwing money at beggars with contempt constitutes Tamasic giving, causing negative karmic reactions.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ॐ तत्सदिति निर्देशो ब्रह्मणस्त्रिविधः स्मृतः |
ब्राह्मणास्तेन वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च विहिताः पुरा || २३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ॐ तत्सदिति निर्देशो ब्रह्मणस्त्रिविधः स्मृतः |
ब्राह्मणास्तेन वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च विहिताः पुरा || २३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
oṃ tatsaditi nirdeśo brahmaṇastrividhaḥ smṛtaḥ |
brāhmaṇāstena vedāśca yajñāśca vihitāḥ purā || 23 ||
verses.word_meanings: oṃ tat sat—OM TAT SAT; iti—thus; nirdeśaḥ—the sacred threefold designation; brahmaṇaḥ—of the Supreme Absolute Truth (Brahman); tri-vidhaḥ—threefold; smṛtaḥ—is declared; brāhmaṇāḥ—the knowers of Brahman; tena—by that; vedāḥ ca—and the Vedic hymns; yajñāḥ ca—and the sacrifices; vihitāḥ—were established; purā—in ancient times.
verses.translation: 'OM TAT SAT'—this has been declared as the sacred threefold designation of the Supreme Absolute Truth (Brahman). By this, in ancient times, the sages, the Vedas, and the sacrifices were ordained.
verses.meaning: The sacred formula 'OM TAT SAT' is the supreme spiritual purifier: It connects every human endeavor with the eternal Parabrahman, dissolving any defects or gunas in sacrifice, penance, and charity.
verses.purport: The sacred formula 'OM TAT SAT' is the supreme spiritual purifier: It connects every human endeavor with the eternal Parabrahman, dissolving any defects or gunas in sacrifice, penance, and charity.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तस्मादोमित्युदाहृत्य यज्ञदानतपःक्रियाः |
प्रवर्तन्ते विधानोक्ताः सततं ब्रह्मवादिनाम् || २४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तस्मादोमित्युदाहृत्य यज्ञदानतपःक्रियाः |
प्रवर्तन्ते विधानोक्ताः सततं ब्रह्मवादिनाम् || २४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
tasmādomityudāhṛtya yajñadānatapaḥkriyāḥ |
pravartante vidhānoktāḥ satataṃ brahmavādinām || 24 ||
verses.word_meanings: tasmāt—therefore; om iti—with the utterance of OM; udāhṛtya—chanting/invoking; yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-kriyāḥ—acts of sacrifice, charity, and austerity; pravartante—commence/begin; vidhāna-uktāḥ—prescribed by scriptural ordinances; satatam—always; brahma-vādinām—of the seekers of Brahman.
verses.translation: Therefore, by always chanting the sacred syllable 'OM', all acts of sacrifice, charity, and austerity prescribed by scriptural injunctions are initiated by the teachers of Brahman.
verses.meaning: 'OM' represents the primordial cosmic vibration of God. Invoking OM at the start of any noble work dedicates the action directly to the Supreme Divine.
verses.purport: 'OM' represents the primordial cosmic vibration of God. Invoking OM at the start of any noble work dedicates the action directly to the Supreme Divine.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तदित्यनभिसन्धाय फलं यज्ञतपःक्रियाः |
दानक्रियाश्च विविधाः क्रियन्ते मोक्षकाङ्क्षिभिः || २५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तदित्यनभिसन्धाय फलं यज्ञतपःक्रियाः |
दानक्रियाश्च विविधाः क्रियन्ते मोक्षकाङ्क्षिभिः || २५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
tadityanabhisandhāya phalaṃ yajñatapaḥkriyāḥ |
dānakriyāśca vividhāḥ kriyante mokṣakāṅkṣibhiḥ || 25 ||
verses.word_meanings: tat iti—with the utterance of 'TAT' (That Transcendence); anabhisandhāya—without desiring; phalam—fruit/reward; yajña-tapaḥ-kriyāḥ—acts of sacrifice and penance; dāna-kriyāḥ ca—and acts of charity; vividhāḥ—various; kriyante—are performed; mokṣa-kāṅkṣibhiḥ—by seekers of liberation.
verses.translation: With the utterance of 'TAT' (That Supreme Reality), diverse acts of sacrifice, austerity, and charity are performed without desire for fruits by seekers of spiritual liberation.
verses.meaning: 'TAT' reminds the seeker that all fruits belong to 'That' (the Supreme Lord), dissolving the ego of doership and ensuring unselfish detachment.
verses.purport: 'TAT' reminds the seeker that all fruits belong to 'That' (the Supreme Lord), dissolving the ego of doership and ensuring unselfish detachment.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सद्भावे साधुभावे च सदित्येतत्प्रयुज्यते |
प्रशस्ते कर्मणि तथा सच्छब्दः पार्थ युज्यते || २६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सद्भावे साधुभावे च सदित्येतत्प्रयुज्यते |
प्रशस्ते कर्मणि तथा सच्छब्दः पार्थ युज्यते || २६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
sadbhāve sādhubhāve ca sadityetatprayujyate |
praśaste karmaṇi tathā sacchabdaḥ pārtha yujyate || 26 ||
verses.word_meanings: sat-bhāve—in the sense of eternal truth/reality; sādhu-bhāve—in the sense of supreme goodness; ca—and; sat iti etat—the word 'SAT'; prayujyate—is applied; praśaste—in auspicious/noble; karmaṇi—action; tathā—likewise; sat-śabdaḥ—the sacred word 'SAT'; pārtha—O Partha (Arjuna); yujyate—is employed.
verses.translation: The word 'SAT' is used to designate eternal Reality (Sat-bhava) and supreme Goodness (Sadhu-bhava); likewise, O Partha, the word 'SAT' is applied to every noble and auspicious action.
verses.meaning: 'SAT' signifies that which is real, eternal, pure, and spiritually beneficial, transforming mundane deeds into immortal offerings.
verses.purport: 'SAT' signifies that which is real, eternal, pure, and spiritually beneficial, transforming mundane deeds into immortal offerings.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यज्ञे तपसि दाने च स्थितिः सदिति चोच्यते |
कर्म चैव तदर्थीयं सदित्येवाभिधीयते || २७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यज्ञे तपसि दाने च स्थितिः सदिति चोच्यते |
कर्म चैव तदर्थीयं सदित्येवाभिधीयते || २७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yajñe tapasi dāne ca sthitiḥ saditi cocyate |
karma caiva tadarthīyaṃ sadityevābhidhīyate || 27 ||
verses.word_meanings: yajñe—in sacrifice; tapasi—in austerity; dāne—in charity; ca—and; sthitiḥ—steadfastness/abiding; sat iti ca ucyate—is also called 'SAT'; karma ca eva—and action indeed; tat-arthīyam—for the sake of the Supreme Lord; sat iti eva—as 'SAT' alone; abhidhīyate—is designated.
verses.translation: Steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity, and charity is also called 'SAT'; and any action performed directly for the sake of the Supreme Lord is likewise designated as 'SAT'.
verses.meaning: Unshakable devotion to spiritual duties and dedicating all works for God (Tadarthiya Karma) are eternal and real (Sat).
verses.purport: Unshakable devotion to spiritual duties and dedicating all works for God (Tadarthiya Karma) are eternal and real (Sat).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अश्रद्धया हुतं दत्तं तपस्तप्तं कृतं च यत् |
असदित्युच्यते पार्थ न च तत्प्रेत्य नो इह || २८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अश्रद्धया हुतं दत्तं तपस्तप्तं कृतं च यत् |
असदित्युच्यते पार्थ न च तत्प्रेत्य नो इह || २८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
aśraddhayā hutaṃ dattaṃ tapastaptaṃ kṛtaṃ ca yat |
asadityucyate pārtha na ca tatpretya no iha || 28 ||
verses.word_meanings: aśraddhayā—without faith; hutam—sacrifice offered in fire; dattam—charity given; tapaḥ taptam—austerity undergone; kṛtam ca yat—and whatever ritual is performed; asat iti ucyate—is declared as 'ASAT' (unreal, fruitless, and transient); pārtha—O Partha; na ca tat—neither that; pretya—hereafter in the next life; no iha—nor in this world.
verses.translation: Whatever sacrifice is offered, charity given, penance performed, or any ritual undertaken without faith is declared as 'ASAT' (fruitless and transient), O Partha. It yields no benefit in this life nor in the life to come.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna seals Chapter 17 by reiterating the supremacy of Faith (Shraddha): Without authentic faith in God, external rituals, philanthropy, and penance remain dead and hollow (Asat), yielding no lasting peace or liberation.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna seals Chapter 17 by reiterating the supremacy of Faith (Shraddha): Without authentic faith in God, external rituals, philanthropy, and penance remain dead and hollow (Asat), yielding no lasting peace or liberation.
